title: A rule-set file's front matter
description: A backbone file schema (ADR-056): the data of one rule set (COR-051 point 2) — its name, its own version, what it inherits, its scope, and one entry per rule carrying the rule's machine fields. The statements are the file's body, one section per rule headed by its id. The join between data and prose, the id rules, origins, successors and inheritance are checked by `project_kit.rule_sets` on top of this shape; inside each rule entry the methodology's container (`pkit`) is read by the container schema and rule (`container.schema.json`, COR-053 point 10). Bound by location — a Markdown file in a place declared to hold rule sets — never by a field. The shape is backbone-owned: it carries no version of its own and is migrated when it changes (COR-010). The `version` key is the rule set's own version, the one inheritors pin.

rule-set.description: The rule set's name: upper-case letters and digits, starting with a letter. Unique among rule sets; every rule id carries it (COR-051 point 3).

version.description: The rule set's own version, semantic-versioned; not its component's. Its major is what an inheriting set pins. A major is required when an accepted rule is withdrawn, superseded or tightened, when an offered extension point is removed, or when a new accepted rule is added (COR-051 point 7).

inherits.description: The rule sets this one inherits, each pinned to a major version: `<SET>@<major>` for a project rule set, `<component>:<SET>@<major>` for a method rule set (COR-051 points 6 and 7).

scope.description: Which artefacts the rules apply to, given as places: repository-relative paths or globs. A consuming component may narrow it (COR-051 point 2).

rules.description: One entry per rule, keyed by its id `RS-<SET>-NNN`. Superseded and withdrawn rules stay with their ids, so a retired id is never reused (COR-051 points 3 and 4).

rule.title: One rule's machine fields (COR-051 points 2, 4 and 5)
rule.description: A rule without a status is proposed and binds nothing. A superseded rule names its successor; no other rule names one.

status.description: `proposed` (the default, binding nothing), `accepted` (binding), `superseded` (replaced by its successor) or `withdrawn` (retired without a successor).

offers.description: Extension points this rule offers, by name; each is cited `RS-<SET>-NNN#<name>`.

fills.description: Extension points of inherited rules that this rule fills, each `RS-<SET>-NNN#<name>`, optionally with the owning component in front. Each point is filled at most once along an inheritance chain (COR-051 point 7).

successor.description: The rule that replaces this superseded one: in the same rule set, or in a set that inherits it (COR-051 point 4).

pkit.description: The methodology's container, which carries the friction block every artefact may carry (COR-050). Its shape is the container schema's (`container.schema.json`) and the container rule's (COR-053 point 10), both applied by the validator; nothing about it is constrained here.

origin.title: Where the rule came from (COR-051 point 5)
origin.description: Either the decider's own words — `date`, `by` and `why` — or a decision record cited as `decision`, for a rule whose reasoning outgrows a line; either may add a `source`. Every accepted rule carries a complete origin. The validator checks completeness, that a cited record exists and is accepted whenever the rule is, and that a source resolves.

decision.description: The decision record that carries the reasoning: `COR-NNN`, `PRJ-NNN`, `ADR-NNN`, or a capability's `<capability>:DEC-NNN`.

source.title: A captured record of where the quoted words were said (COR-051 point 5)
source.description: An anchor of a kind that some capability registers with a resolver (COR-050 point 2), written as its kind and value. A kind with no installed resolver is reported as an unresolved kind, never silently passed.

kind.description: The anchor kind, as the capability that resolves it registers it.

pin.description: A rule set and the major version inherited: `<SET>@<major>`, with `<component>:` in front for a method rule set.

rule-id.description: `RS-<SET>-NNN`: the family prefix, the rule set's name, and a number of at least three digits (zero-padded below 100).

rule-reference.description: A rule, `RS-<SET>-NNN`, optionally with its owning component in front.

point-name.description: An extension point's name, in kebab-case.

point-reference.description: An extension point a rule offers, `RS-<SET>-NNN#<name>`, optionally with the rule's owning component in front.
